title: OpenBao Secret Access Flow
summary: Applications authenticate with an auth method, receive a token bound to policies, read secrets from engines, and every request is audited.

nodes.label: Client / App
nodes.detail: Authenticates, then uses the returned token on subsequent API calls. Tokens are short-lived and renewable.

nodes.label: AppRole Auth
nodes.detail: AppRole is a machine auth method. Role ID identifies the app, secret ID is the credential, delivered separately and often single-use.

nodes.label: Policy
nodes.detail: HCL rules grant capabilities such as read or list on secret paths. Tokens receive only the policies attached to their role.

nodes.label: Token
nodes.detail: Issued after login with a TTL and policy set. Requests without a valid token are denied by default.

nodes.label: KV Secrets Engine
nodes.detail: Key-value engine mounted at a path. KV v2 keeps versions, so secrets can be rolled back or destroyed.

nodes.label: Encryption Barrier
nodes.detail: All data is encrypted before reaching storage. The barrier is opened only when the instance is unsealed.

nodes.label: Raft Storage
nodes.detail: Integrated Raft storage replicates encrypted data across nodes with one active leader and standbys.

nodes.label: Audit Device
nodes.detail: Logs every request and response with sensitive values hashed. Typically written to a file or syslog for review.

steps.title: App logs in
steps.text: The app presents its AppRole role ID and secret ID to the auth method.

steps.title: Policies are attached
steps.text: The role maps to policies that define which paths and operations are allowed.

steps.title: Token returned
steps.text: The app receives a short-lived token and uses it for later calls, renewing as needed.

steps.title: Secret is read
steps.text: The app reads a path in the KV engine; the policy check passes or the call is denied.

steps.title: Encrypted storage and audit
steps.text: Data passes through the barrier into Raft storage, and the request is written to the audit device.
